correctness.rationale: Chefles gives the exact LOCC detection condition: product state in W_k=orthogonal to the other two but not psi_k. Independent triple makes W_k dim2, while psi_k functional has one-dimensional kernel spanned by nonzero C. With independent D, all candidates sC+tD detect iff t!=0, and are product iff det(sC+tD)=s²det C+st tr(adj(C)D)+t²detD=0. Over complex numbers this homogeneous quadratic has a projective zero at t!=0 unless its sole double root is t=0; that exceptional case is exactly det C=0, mixed term zero and detD nonzero. A line with this intersection is tangent to the smooth Segre quadric; the condition is invariant under changing adapted bases. Independent explicit C=[[1,0],[0,0]], D=[[0,1],[1,0]] gives determinant -t²; source Bell-pair example supplies a physical witness. This is exact algebra; random triples are not an infinite proof.
residual_risks: Finite computations are only corroboration; general statement rests on analytic proof and stated hypotheses.

Yang et al. 2015 identify triple-state counterexamples. Neither inspected relevant primary theorem states the explicit iff triple scalar tangency test. The result is a synthesis/specialization of known detector and Segre concepts; equivalent matrix-pencil tangency formulation could preexist and is a clear residual risk.

value.rationale: Three pure two-qubit states are the smallest nontrivial case where LOCC unambiguous identification can fail despite linear independence. Converting an existential product-state search into an exact projective tangency condition and three explicit determinant tests is a motivated classification/decision procedure in this boundary case; it distinguishes tangent, secant and contained-line cases. No optimization of success probabilities is claimed.
